subject: Performance MAP: regional latency sweep & routing playbook
messages:
From: Maya Singh <maya.s@cloudfusion.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@cloudfusion.com
Date: 2026-07-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Kickoff: perf MAP & tests for POC

Camila —

Thanks for the intro call yesterday. We want to capture a simple Mutual Action Plan (MAP) that includes a short performance evaluation plan for the POC. High-level asks from our side:

- Regional latency sweep (US / EU / APAC) measuring p50/p95 and tail behavior.
- Throughput and sustained concurrency tests (target: sustain 1k TPS, concurrency up to 64 across client workers).
- TTFT (time-to-first-token) under cold and warmed caches (TTFT target: <100ms warm, <250ms cold).
- Failover & routing playbook: if the primary region spikes above p95 SLA, automatic routing to secondary region and model-fallback behavior.

Go/no-go criteria for our product team: p95 latency < 250ms (regional), sustained throughput within 10% of expected cost budget, and predictable TTFT for cold starts. We can relax numbers if you recommend different thresholds based on the model.

Deliverables we expect: a short MAP (milestones + owners), a test harness (or instructions) we can run from our infra, and a CSV with raw measurements. Target close timeline: execute evaluation runs in the window 2026-07-06 to 2026-07-10 and have an exec readout by 2026-07-15.

I attached our perf template and a small sample payload. Can you confirm resources and a proposed schedule?

Thanks,
Maya Singh
Product & POC Lead, CloudFusion

Attachment: cloudfusion_perf_template.xlsx (spreadsheet with sample payloads and desired metrics)

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Singh <maya.s@cloudfusion.com>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-01T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff: perf MAP & tests for POC

Maya —

Thanks — this is clear and actionable. I attached a draft MAP (redwood_map_v1.xlsx) with milestones and owners + a short routing-playbook-draft.md. High level schedule I propose:

- 2026-07-02: finalize MAP & test plan (owners: me / Sergio)
- 2026-07-06: baseline sweep (low QPS) across US/EU/APAC — collect p50/p95 and TTFT (cold/warm)
- 2026-07-07: ramp throughput tests (ramp to 1k TPS sustained with concurrency steps: 8, 16, 32, 64)
- 2026-07-08: failover + multi-region routing rehearsals (simulate region outage, model fallback)
- 2026-07-10: final run + raw CSV delivery

Quick notes: for TTFT we will capture first-byte and first-token timing separately; we will also run a short cold-start matrix (container spin-up) to estimate worst-case TTFT. For routing playbook, draft includes: routing by latency SLO, circuit-breaker triggers at 95th percentile, and model-fallback to a quantized variant if latency budget is breached.

Please confirm the sample payload in your template is the right shape (we used one sentence + metadata). Also tell us which regions you can run probes from — if you can run from k8s in GCP/AWS that helps mirror production routing.

I booked a 30-min check on 2026-07-05 to finalize the MAP — invite coming.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_map_v1.xlsx, routing-playbook-draft.md

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-02T09:00:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: test design and responsibilities for CloudFusion MAP

Team —

Draft test plan and owners below; please reply with any objections by EOD. We need clear tooling and measurement points so the external CSV matches our dashboard metrics.

Test harness: use k6 for HTTP-level load; wrap in a small runner that records: request start, first byte, first token (inferred from chunk/frame start), request end, and token counts. Store raw lines to CSV.

Regions / vantage points:
- us-east-1 (primary) — run 8 client workers, ramp to target.
- eu-west-1 — run 6 client workers.
- ap-southeast-1 — run 4 client workers (simulate higher RTT).

Metrics: p50, p95, p99 latencies (ms), TTFT_warm(ms), TTFT_cold(ms), tokens/sec throughput, server-side CPU/GPU utilization, and model KV cache hit-rate.

Concurrency plan: seq of sustained windows 60s at concurrency levels: 8, 16, 32, 64 (collect steady-state metrics at each). Also run 10x short spike tests to exercise autoscaling.

Failover scenario: induce 30% packet loss/emulated latency in us-east and observe routing to eu-west; measure time-to-divert and p95 delta. Also test model-fallback to quantized variant (smaller memory footprint) under capacity pressure.

Responsibilities:
- Sergio: run the cluster-side workload and collect server metrics + orchestrate model-fallback variants.
- Neha: run the distributed clients and aggregate CSVs, produce the per-region dashboard snapshots.
- Camila: own MAP updates, exec readout materials, coordinate with CloudFusion ops.

Deliverable timeline matches the MAP Camila sent to the customer. I left a short doc in the drive link with k6 snippets and measurement hooks.

Camila

From: Rajiv Patel <rajiv.p@cloudfusion.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Maya Singh <maya.s@cloudfusion.com>
Date: 2026-07-09T14:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Performance MAP: regional latency sweep & routing playbook

Camila / team —

We completed an initial sweep using your runner (thanks Sergio & Neha). Attached is latency_results_2026-07.csv with raw lines. Quick summary of the first pass (single-worker baseline, warm cache):

- US (us-east-1): p50=38ms, p95=120ms, p99=210ms, TTFT_warm=42ms.
- EU (eu-west-1): p50=54ms, p95=145ms, p99=260ms, TTFT_warm=60ms.
- APAC (ap-southeast-1): p50=115ms, p95=320ms, p99=680ms, TTFT_warm=140ms.

Notes: APAC shows the expected RTT impact; p95 is outside your target in APAC. Under a 32-concurrency sustained run we saw throughput stall at ~720 TPS for the model variant we tested; GPU was approaching memory pressure and the KV cache hit-rate dropped. We haven't yet run the cold-start matrix (will do that during the next window).

Failover rehearsal: when we injected 250ms extra latency to us-east, routing to eu-west happened on the 2nd detected breach (as configured) and the end-to-end p95 increased by ~30ms during the diversion window. We also exercised the quantized fallback; it reduced p95 by ~40ms but decreased semantic similarity scores by ~3% in a small eval — worth reviewing with your product folks.

Attached: latency_results_2026-07.csv (raw), perf-notes-apac.txt (ops observations).

Rajiv
CloudFusion — Infra

Date: 2026-07-12T16:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Performance MAP: regional latency sweep & routing playbook — next steps + close timeline

Maya / Rajiv —

Thanks for the data and notes — very helpful. Summary and next steps so we can close the MAP this week:

1) APAC workstream (owner: Sergio) — optimize routing + consider an edge POP nearer ap-south-1; re-run sweep focusing on p95 reduction in APAC by 2026-07-14.
2) Throughput tuning (owner: Neha) — test quantization profiles and sequence batching to hit sustained 1k TPS; provide a configuration recommendation by 2026-07-14.
3) Cold-start matrix (owner: Rajiv & Sergio) — run cold-starts from each region and capture TTFT_cold; deliver CSV by 2026-07-13.
4) Routing playbook finalization (owner: Camila) — include circuit-breaker thresholds, detection windows, and fallback model mapping; deliver final playbook and exec slide by 2026-07-15.

Proposed exec readout: 2026-07-15 10:00 PT — 20-min readout + 10-min Q&A. If that works for you we'll send the calendar invite.

Notes on trade-offs: quantized fallback reduces latency but can produce a small dip in semantic fidelity (~2–4% on our eval set) — recommend a staged fallback: first route requests to secondary region (if available) and only use quantized fallback when capacity is the limiting factor.

I'll attach a short slide with the MAP milestones and the recommended go/no-go checks for the POC close. Once we have the final CSVs I'll produce the consolidated dashboard export for your leadership.

Thanks again — close-looking good.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Attachments: routing-playbook-draft.md, redwood_map_v1.xlsx
